name: IEC general code converter (X/Y)
summary: IEC element marked X/Y, the general coder converting one code, named X, into another, named Y.
description: The general coder qualifier X/Y is replaced on a real symbol by the names of the input and output codes, such as BIN/GRAY or DEC/BCD. Where the codes are not standard, inputs and outputs carry numbers and a table on the drawing gives the relationship. TI's overview also shows coders embedded in larger symbols to produce affecting inputs for dependency notation.

On control and protection logic drawings, a code converter may represent a lookup in a PLC or a hardware coder converting a selector position code into commands. Including the conversion table is essential because the X/Y label alone does not define the mapping for non-standard codes.
The element does not state propagation timing or behaviour for invalid input codes. State those in notes where they matter.
readingNotes: Replace X and Y with code names on a real symbol.
Look for a conversion table on the sheet.
drawingChecklist: Name both codes or provide a table.
Number inputs and outputs consistently with the table.
distinction: Specific coders such as BIN/OCT or BCD/7SEG are instances of this general form with standard code names.
